messages:
prashant: Heads up — after publishing the exports update, our Next.js SSR sample on Vercel Edge throws: "TypeError: RedwoodClient is not a constructor"

lydia: Damn. Which entry did the bundle resolve to?

prashant: It resolved to the CJS path during SSR bundling. package.json now has conditionals: import -> ./dist/index.mjs, require -> ./dist/index.cjs. Rollup/Vite pulled the CJS file into the edge bundle.

nate: If the CJS build doesn't keep named exports, `import { RedwoodClient }` will fail when the runtime sees only a default/init export.

prashant: Workaround that fixed our sample: add a vite/rollup alias for SSR: `alias: { '@redwood/inference': '/node_modules/@redwood/inference/dist/index.mjs' }` and set `resolve.mainFields = ['module','browser','main']`.

lydia: Long-term: we should (A) remove the stray CJS shim and rebuild CJS with preserved named exports, and (B) add explicit subpath export `./edge` -> `./dist/index.mjs` so bundlers targeting edge don't fallback.

nate: Also add a CI publish-time check: spawn node (CJS) require and dynamic import (ESM) assert both shapes contain RedwoodClient.

ci-bot: created issue RED-DEVEX-4302: "fix(exports): edge/ssr interop + publish checks" assigned to prashant

prashant: I'll open the patch to clean the shim and add the edge subpath. I'll also add a tiny Vercel Edge repro in infra-samples for CI.

lydia: I'll update the DevEx guide with the SSR resolve snippet and callout for Edge runtimes.

nate: Thanks — let's prioritize, this breaks onboarding samples.
